title: Cell-type-specific transcriptome-wide association study using scPrediXcan framework
author: Zhou, Sumner, et al.
materials: scPrediXcan requires a Linux or MacOS system with a minimum 16 RAM available; for full training, 64 RAM is suggested. It also requires Conda, Python, Nextflow, and the deep learning package Pytorch. This step outlines how to create a Conda environment (named scPrediXcan) and install the software packages needed (above) on Linux or MacOS. The user must install and initialize Conda before the first step.1.For Linux: Run the following code in the terminal to create a parent folder named scTWAS for all downloaded data and generated results. It will also create a new environment in Conda with the and activate the environment for running scPrediXcan.# Make project parent filemkdir scTWAScd scTWAS# Clone repositories for ctPred traininggit clone https://github.com/hakyimlab/scPrediXcan.git# Create and activate conda environment for Linuxconda env create -f scPrediXcan/scPrediXcan_env.ymlconda activate scPrediXcanAlternatives: For MacOS, use -f scPrediXcan/scPrediXcan_mac_env.yml for conda environment creation.# Make project parent filemkdir scTWAScd scTWAS# Clone repositories for ctPred traininggit clone https://github.com/hakyimlab/scPrediXcan.git# Create and activate conda environment for MacOSconda env create -f scPrediXcan/scPrediXcan_mac_env.ymlconda activate scPrediXcan2.Clone the PredictDb-nextflow and S-PrediXcan3 repositories and create a folder to store the results.# Clone repositories for l-ctPred training and S-PrediXcangit clone https://github.com/hakyimlab/PredictDb-nextflow.gitgit clone https://github.com/hakyimlab/MetaXcanmkdir ResultsNote: At the end of Software preparation, you should have a parent folder named scTWAS on your local hard drive that contains four subfolders: scPrediXcan, PredictDb-nextflow, MetaXcan, and Results.

steps.title: Set up software environment
steps.instruction: Install required software, create project directory, clone repositories, and create a Conda environment for scPrediXcan.

substeps.instruction: Ensure a Linux or macOS system with at least 16 GB RAM (64 GB RAM recommended for full training) and that Conda is installed and initialized.
Open a terminal and run:
mkdir scTWAS
cd scTWAS
git clone https://github.com/hakyimlab/scPrediXcan.git
For Linux: conda env create -f scPrediXcan/scPrediXcan_env.yml
For macOS: conda env create -f scPrediXcan/scPrediXcan_mac_env.yml
conda activate scPrediXcan
git clone https://github.com/hakyimlab/PredictDb-nextflow.git
git clone https://github.com/hakyimlab/MetaXcan.git
mkdir Results
Verify that the scTWAS folder now contains the subfolders: scPrediXcan, PredictDb-nextflow, MetaXcan, and Results.

steps.title: Download example dataset (optional)
steps.instruction: Obtain the toy example data from Zenodo and extract it into the project folder.

substeps.instruction: Run the following commands in the scTWAS directory:
zenodo_get 18124207
tar -xzf Download_dataset.tar.gz && rm Download_dataset.tar.gz
This creates scTWAS/Download_dataset containing the example files.
If the download fails, manually download the archive from https://zenodo.org/records/18124207 and extract it to /scTWAS/Download_dataset.

steps.title: Prepare single‑cell expression matrix
steps.instruction: Process user‑provided or example scRNA‑seq count data into pseudobulk individual‑by‑gene matrices per cell type, applying quality‑control filters.

substeps.instruction: Filter cells to keep only those expressing more than 200 gene features, and retain only gene features that appear in at least three cells.
Remove doublets and triplets using the DoubletDecon tool.
Exclude non‑coding genes that are absent from the Enformer‑derived epigenomic features file (provided in the key resources).
Split the filtered cell‑by‑gene matrix by cell‑type labels, producing one matrix per cell type.
For each cell type, aggregate counts across all cells belonging to the same individual to obtain an individual‑by‑gene count matrix (pseudobulk).
Ensure that gene identifiers are consistent between the pseudobulk matrix and the Enformer feature file; if necessary, align using gene names (column name must be ‘gene_name’ in both files).

steps.title: Create training file for ctPred
steps.instruction: Merge expression percentiles with Enformer epigenomic features to generate the ctPred training CSV.

substeps.instruction: Load the pseudobulk expression matrix (e.g., ./Download_dataset/Acinar_normcounts.csv) and the Enformer epigenomics file (./Download_dataset/Gene_epigenomics_v0.csv).
Run the data preparation script:
python scPrediXcan/Scripts/ctPred/data_prep.py \
--exp './Download_dataset/Acinar_normcounts.csv' \
--epi './Download_dataset/Gene_epigenomics_v0.csv' \
--output './Download_dataset/training_cell.csv'
The script will:
a) Calculate mean expression across individuals.
b) Convert mean expression to rank‑based percentiles.
c) Merge the percentiles with the epigenomics file, producing a CSV with 5 316 columns (generic index ID, gene name, 5 313 epigenomic features, and expression percentile).
The resulting file (training_cell.csv) is saved in ./Download_dataset and will be used as input for ctPred model training.
